HANDOFF for DrWrinch

Source: HANDOFF.md

Last touched: 2026-10-27. Read PLAN_decision_rule.md next. It records what changed in the paper between 2026-08-29 and 2026-10-19, the four choices Jake made on 2026-10-27, the tests written before the code, and the edits the paper repository needs once this version is on GitHub.

2026-11-11: the app and documentation follow the paper’s current wording

Jake asked Claude, in a cloud session, whether the package and the app match the paper as it stands (arXiv v3, tag arxiv-2026-11-06 in the paper repository). Claude ran the package against the paper’s own code in tests/*.R and against replications/<study>/results.csv. Every number the paper reports agrees. Where the two differ, at extreme counts, the package is the accurate one: at 0 and 25 with a bias of 1.5 the package gives 6.9474e-11, the paper’s binom_bf_weighted() gives 6.9869e-11, and a sum over two million points gives 6.9474e-11.

Jake then asked for four changes, made on the branch claude/serene-ramanujan-ebm3vl and merged into main at his request the same day. They are version 0.0.2.2, and NEWS.md lists them:

  • README, inst/CITATION, and the app’s About tab cite the paper’s current title.
  • README and the app use the paper’s phrase “Bayes factor range.” The helper describe_range() in inst/shiny/R/helpers.R writes the sentence on the Result tab.
  • The worst-case card prints no Kass and Raftery verdict. The helper worst_case_status() says whether the value is above the second threshold.
  • The sidebar and the About tab say that a weighted observation is entered by adding its weight to the count.

Checked: the tests were written first and failed; with the changes all 148 test blocks (1154 expectations) pass under R 4.3.3, and the app’s Result tab showed the new sentences in a headless browser. Not checked: devtools::check(), the pkgdown build, and the hosted app, which this session’s network could not reach.

The same day Jake asked for a way to deploy the app without his own computer. .github/workflows/deploy-shiny.yaml is new. It runs only when someone presses “Run workflow” on the Actions page. It installs DrWrinch from GitHub at the commit being deployed, runs the tests, and sources deploy.R. It needs two repository secrets, SHINYAPPS_TOKEN and SHINYAPPS_SECRET, from the shinyapps.io dashboard (Account, then Tokens). source("deploy.R") from a computer still works as before.

Jake added the secrets and ran the workflow (run 43116816354). The secrets worked: rsconnect found the application. The run then stopped while rsconnect listed the app’s packages, because renv will not snapshot when a package named in an installed package’s LinkingTo field is absent, and the binary installs had left out cpp11, which tidyr and isoband link to. Claude added a step that installs every such missing package.

The next run (43118293863) passed that point, uploaded the bundle, and failed while shinyapps.io built the image: “Unsupported url scheme: RSPM/src/contrib/remotes_2.5.0.tar.gz”. The manifest named the repository RSPM for remotes and gave no address for it. Claude changed the deploy step to name the repositories itself, to print where the manifest says each package comes from, and to stop before any upload if a package from a repository has no web address. Claude ran that check in a session with no route to the repositories, where it stopped as written. Whether the run after this fix succeeds is not yet known, and the hosted app is unchanged: the failed build did not replace it, as far as the log shows.

Left as they were, for Jake to decide:

  • When the counts favor the rival, bf_worst_case() holds the rival at one half, as the paper’s closed form does. One half is then not the rival’s most favorable share, and the value can exceed the uniform-weights value (two and five: 0.22 against 0.17). The app’s range sentence orders the two numbers by size for that reason.
  • .dw_needed in inst/shiny/global.R stays at 0.0.2.1, because the app calls no function that 0.0.2.1 lacks.
  • R/DrWrinch-package.R, the help pages, and the vignette do not use “Bayes factor range.” roxygen2 was not available to rebuild the help pages.
  • “At least provisionally” stays in the package’s wording of the rule. POINT.md in the paper repository uses it; Paper/evalues.qmd does not.

What DrWrinch is

The R package implementing Lopez, Bowers, and Gajardo Cooper (2026), “Fully specified Bayes factors for process tracing.” The paper is in ~/repos/fully_specified_bf and is the source of truth for notation and methods. The package is named after Dorothy Maud Wrinch (1894–1976), whose joint papers with Harold Jeffreys developed the framework that became Jeffreys’s theory of Bayes factors. The companion package DrBristol (~/repos/DrBristol) implements p-value methods for the same problems; the two stay separate.

State of the package, 2026-10-27

Version 0.0.2.1, commit f3c04a8, pushed to main on 2026-10-27. All 134 tests (1101 expectations) succeed with no warnings, and devtools::check() reports 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes. The pkgdown workflow rebuilt the site from that commit; its previous run, on 2026-08-30, had failed. The hosted app runs 0.0.2.1. Both tabs render the running example: Bayes factors of 20.67 and 2.73, under which a researcher following the rule sets the rival aside, and a decision that one re-coding or a bias of 1.01 would change.

Under the paper’s rule, a researcher sets the rival aside, at least provisionally, when the uniform-weights Bayes factor is 20 or more and the worst-case Bayes factor is above 1. The exported functions follow it:

  • bf_uniform_weights(y_W, y_R, omega), in R/bf_uniform_weights.R.
  • bf_worst_case(y_W, y_R, omega, a1, b1), in R/bf_worst_case.R. Under bias it divides by the largest probability any rival share gives the counts, which moves below a share of one half once omega > y_W / y_R (Jake’s decision of 2026-10-27; the paper’s five affected table cells are to be recomputed to match). When y_W < y_R the rival stays at one half, as in the paper’s closed form.
  • bf_rescaled(), in R/bf_rescaled.R.
  • bf_uniform_weights_finite() and bf_worst_case_finite(), in R/bf_finite.R, for an archive of known size.
  • sens_bias() and sens_coding(), in R/sens_bias.R and R/sens_coding.R. Each returns the tipping point for each condition of the rule and the smaller of the two.
  • run_app(), in R/run_app.R.

Removed in this version, without deprecation because no one else uses the package: bf_binomial(), bf_urn(), sens_urn(), sens_binomial(), bf_separated(), separation_g(), bf_separated_bias(), and the deprecation helper. BiasedUrn, ggplot2, and dplyr left DESCRIPTION.

The Shiny app (inst/shiny/) takes two thresholds, opens the Result tab with what the rule decides, and on the Sensitivity tab reports the coding and bias tipping points under the rule beside one plot of both Bayes factors against the bias. .dw_needed in inst/shiny/global.R is 0.0.2.1.

The paper repository

The paper still sources its own tests/*.R. Two cross-checks in its tests/bf_weighted.R call DrWrinch::bf_binomial() and DrWrinch::bf_urn(), so rendering the paper or the supplement, or running the replications, will stop with an error as soon as the paper’s renv library installs this version. PLAN_decision_rule.md lists those fixes, the supplement’s reproduction section rewrite, the renv.lock update, and the five worst-case cells. The current arXiv preprint’s reproduction section calls removed functions, so the next arXiv replacement is what brings the preprint and the package back into agreement.

Deployment failures and their fixes

  • Install DrWrinch from GitHub on this machine before deploying (2026-10-27). rsconnect records the locally installed DrWrinch in the manifest, and shinyapps.io builds the image from that record. With an older local copy (0.0.1.9000 then), the image held the old version, global.R fell back to install_github() at start-up, and that anonymous call failed with GitHub’s API rate limit (HTTP 403, 60 requests an hour shared by every app on the server’s address), so the app failed to start. After remotes::install_github( "bowers-illinois-edu/DrWrinch") here and a second deploy, the image held 0.0.2.1 and the app started without contacting GitHub.

  • Stale GITHUB_PAT in ~/.Renviron (commented out 2026-05-19, with a note pointing to https://github.com/settings/tokens for a fresh one). If remotes::install_github ever falls back to anonymous unexpectedly, check that this token still works.

  • shinyapps.io’s “401 fetching GitHub” failure mode is almost always a stale OAuth cache, not a missing PAT. The toggle-on / toggle-off cycle in Posit Authentication is the fix.

  • shinyapps.io’s “stale DrWrinch / function-not-found” failure mode (hit and fixed 2026-06-22). shinyapps installs DrWrinch into the read-only system library (/usr/lib/R) at image-build time from its manifest, and that copy can lag GitHub HEAD. A runtime install_github cannot overwrite it (mv ... Permission denied, “cannot remove earlier installation, is it in use?”), so the app silently keeps the old version and errors on any newer function (this session: 'sens_coding' is not an exported object). The symptom is a tab-level “An error has occurred” with the plots still rendering, and the real cause is only visible via rsconnect::showLogs(). Fix in inst/shiny/global.R: install the required version into a writable, session-local library (tempdir()) placed FIRST on .libPaths(), shadowing the stale system copy. Check the installed version with packageVersion() — NOT requireNamespace(), which loads the old namespace and then blocks library() from picking up the reinstall. The GitHub download and build succeed at runtime; only the install location has to be writable. Each cold start spends about 30 seconds on this install. When the required version changes, bump .dw_needed in global.R.

  • rsconnect refuses to bundle locally-installed packages that lack RemoteType metadata. Trying to dodge GitHub via a local tarball doesn’t work cleanly; the right workarounds are

    1. fix the OAuth cache (what worked this session), (b) R-universe.

  • The Shiny app pulls DrWrinch from GitHub on shinyapps.io cold start via the install_github stanza in inst/shiny/global.R, about 30 seconds per cold start. Local development skips it, because devtools::load_all() has already loaded the current version.

Still open

  • inst/CITATION points to the arXiv preprint (arXiv:2606.16683). Add the journal DOI when the paper is published.
  • The app has no shinytest2 snapshot tests. The helpers and the reactive graph are tested through testthat and shiny::testServer().
  • GitHub authentication is switched off in Posit’s settings. Publishing to Posit Cloud would need it switched on again.
